markdown_report:
### Insights and directions

The starting idea yields three insights. First, a zero-initialized residual preserves SASRec’s initial predictions, enabling a controlled architectural extension. Second, a causal five-item window explicitly represents recent evidence, addressing the reported persistence of older interests. Third, neither recency nor embedding coherence establishes current intent, compatibility, or additional usefulness.

The literature suggests three complementary insights. CLSR, TLSRec, and PAN establish adaptive long/short-term fusion precedents, reducing the proposed gate’s originality. Scarcelli et al. motivate sequence-aware perturbations; the supplied Pandey et al. summary cautions that masking sensitivity can reflect unfamiliar inputs. Subbiah et al. and Krichene–Rendle motivate separating sampled-ranking behavior from catalog behavior: training margins cannot substitute for pinned validation HR@10.

These insights organize three directions: controlled recent-history representations, matched attribution diagnostics, and evidence-grounded recommendation judgments. CoDeR+ motivates distinguishing sustained shifts from fluctuations. Available titles, descriptions, and timestamps can support interpretation; unavailable ratings, reviews, compatibility attributes, and simulator traits cannot.

### Framework

| Layer | Existing approach | Proposed extension | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Representation | SASRec plus global recent residual | Unit-normalized item pooling with learned scalar | Pool magnitude already encodes coherence |
| Diagnosis | Embedding geometry and sampled margins | Matched residual ablation, gate controls, history perturbations | Sensitivity does not identify causal intent |
| Selection | Four-category macro validation HR@10 | Matched initialization, schedules, and tuning allowance | Adaptive selection can overfit validation |

### Candidate ideas

Scores are originality/potential/code difficulty, each out of 10; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each assessment explicitly covers all three dimensions.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Coherence-gated recent residual | 3/4/3 | Originality: specific lightweight combination; potential: testable parameterization; difficulty: small branch | Originality: established fusion precedents; potential: redundant coherence statistic and nonclosing gate; difficulty: causal masking and controls |
| Learned two-window residual mixture | 3/6/4 | Originality: adapts the starting residual; potential: models persistence; difficulty: reuses embeddings | Originality: established timescale fusion; potential: greater selection variance; difficulty: additional gates and ablations |
| Perturbation-guided residual regularization | 5/6/6 | Originality: connects attribution and training; potential: explicit dependence control; difficulty: standard tensor operations | Originality: related consistency objectives; potential: potentially incorrect invariances; difficulty: extra forward passes |
| **Unit-normalized recent residual** | **2/6/3** | Originality: controlled revision; potential: establishes whether recent pooling helps; difficulty: minimal implementation | Originality: familiar pooling; potential: cannot establish specific purpose; difficulty: export parity and matched experiments |

### Selected idea

At 10% progress, prioritize the **unit-normalized recent residual** before adaptive gating. For n unit embeddings with mean m and distinct-pair cosine c, ||m||²=[1+(n−1)c]/n. Consequently, the original g=(1+c)/2 contains no information beyond magnitude and length; for five items g≥0.375, and orthogonal items give g=0.5. Applying it compounds coherence-dependent amplitude. Unequal raw norms break this identity and add another confound.

```text
h = SASRec(sequence)
for position t:
    E = embeddings(last five nonpadding items through t)
    U = E / clamp(norm(E), min=epsilon)
    m = mean(U), or zero for an empty window
    z[t] = h[t] + alpha * m
mask padding outputs; alpha starts at zero
score using existing item embeddings
```

Keep alpha unconstrained: negative values subtract the recent direction. At initialization, branch embedding gradients vanish while alpha can receive gradients. Shared embeddings can subsequently alter both direction and coherence; normalization does not eliminate this optimization issue [Cosine Pitfalls].

Preserve routing, splits, seeds, and defaults. Compare SASRec, original raw-mean residual, normalized residual, and the original coherence gate under equal budgets. Use training-only RMS matching for constant-scale controls. Conditional follow-ups include length-stratified shuffled gates, magnitude/length gates, normalized pooled directions, and separate stop-gradient ablations; detachment is an optimization intervention, not semantic evidence [SimSiam]. Frozen reference embeddings offer stronger geometry controls.

Share representations across training, predictor generation, and diagnosis. Track alpha, c, gate distributions, norms, near-zero means, and residual/backbone ratios. Select only by pinned macro validation HR@10; report component ablations separately. Matched comparisons, paired user bootstrap intervals, and export-parity checks strengthen interpretation but do not remove selection bias. No improvement is established by the supplied evidence.

idea.description: Replace the proposed coherence gate with a controlled five-item residual: normalize each nonpadding item embedding, average the causal window, and add it to SASRec through a zero-initialized learned scalar. Retain the original raw residual and coherence gate as experimental controls.
idea.motivation: The diagnosis suggests that recent coherent interests deserve investigation, but the original gate cannot close for a five-item window and duplicates information already present in normalized mean magnitude. A simpler residual can establish whether recent pooling helps before adding adaptive fusion. It cannot infer current purpose, ownership, compatibility, satisfied needs, or unobserved user traits.
idea.implementation_notes: Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], all four dataset routes, existing splits, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and SASREC_EPOCHS default 200. Write artifacts beneath the trial directory and train on one GPU. Use only public histories, timestamps, titles, and descriptions; preserve unavailable metadata fields without fabrication. At every nonpadding position, include the current observed item and at most four preceding nonpadding items, never future items. Normalize each embedding by max(L2 norm, 1e-8), average available vectors without normalizing the mean, and return zero for an empty window. A singleton contributes its normalized vector. Mask padding outputs. For diagnostic cosine calculations, exclude padding and diagonal pairs; report coherence as null for windows with fewer than two vectors or numerically zero vectors. Initialize alpha exactly to zero and leave it unconstrained, recording negative values rather than interpreting it automatically as positive interest. Keep the baseline loss, optimizer, batching, training-negative sampling, truncation, and checkpoint schedule unchanged for the first comparison. Use the same branch feature scale in training and inference; the normalized residual has a different scale from raw pooling, so report norms and learned alpha. Compare four configurations: SASRec, learned raw-mean residual, learned unit-mean residual, and unit-mean residual multiplied by the original coherence gate. Copy identical backbone weights, initialize alpha identically, and use separate explicit random generators for initialization, minibatch order, negatives, and backbone dropout so branch changes do not shift shared randomness. Predeclare a maximum of 10,800 GPU-seconds per configuration, including all four categories, diagnostics, debugging, and failures; the total cap is 43,200 GPU-seconds. Stop a configuration at its allocation if necessary, record unfinished epochs, and report both matched-step and equal-compute comparisons. Use the same existing checkpoint evaluation schedule and selection rule for every configuration, resolving validation ties by the earliest checkpoint. Also report the last checkpoint completed by every configuration at a common training step. If category checkpoints are selected independently, apply that same rule to every configuration and disclose it. Optional additional controls must replace planned configurations within the budget rather than silently expanding search: use a fixed gate computed before validation from training-only RMS matching, shuffled gates within exact window-length groups, magnitude-and-length gates, pooled-direction normalization with epsilon thresholding, and separate stop-gradient interventions on gate, pooled vector, and both. Shuffling should leave singleton and empty-window handling unchanged. Detaching the gate does not freeze shared embedding geometry; a frozen training-only reference is a stronger control. Update the predictor writer to serialize and reconstruct the exact architecture, alpha, normalization epsilon, and window size. Compare exported and in-memory evaluation-mode scores within atol=1e-6 and rtol=1e-5 on identical histories/candidates; verify rankings, routing, padding, truncation, and checkpoint loading, investigating any ranking mismatch. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device) and run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions. view.model must remain the trained module; item_emb, log2feats, and predict_score must match its actual representation. Adapt residual decomposition to alpha times the implemented normalized branch, retaining existing alignment, sampled-margin, and gradient-finiteness probes. Add alpha, raw/unit/pooled norms, coherence by window length, gate statistics for gated controls, near-zero means, residual/backbone norm ratios, and component margin contributions. These remain descriptive training diagnostics. Preserve the pinned evaluator with 200 validation users/category, 99 unique negatives, and evaluation seed 42. If per-user validation outputs are exposed, save paired hit differences and bootstrap users within category using seed 42 and 2,000 resamples, then equally average the four category differences. Intervals condition on trained checkpoints and fixed candidates and exclude training-seed variability and adaptive-selection bias. Keep full-catalog unseen-item diagnostics for the twenty training users separate from benchmark HR@10. No hidden test access, external datasets, pretrained weights, or evaluator changes.
idea.pseudocode:
epsilon = 1e-8
alpha = Parameter(0.0)
H = causal_sasrec(sequence)
for each batch row and position t:
    if sequence[t] == 0:
        Z[t] = 0
        continue
    ids = last_nonpadding(sequence[:t+1], count=5)
    E = item_emb(ids)
    U = E / clamp(l2_norm(E, axis=-1, keepdim=True), min=epsilon)
    M = mean(U, axis=0) if len(ids) else zeros_like(H[t])
    Z[t] = H[t] + alpha * M
return Z
# Use the identical function in training, exported prediction, and diagnosis.
# Optional original-gate control: for n >= 2 compute distinct-pair cosine C;
# for singleton use C=0; for empty history return zero; multiply M by (1+C)/2.
# Report near-zero embeddings and exclude undefined cosines from diagnostics.

originality.positive: Provides a precise, controlled revision of the starting residual and exposes the algebraic redundancy in the proposed gate.
originality.negative: Normalized pooling and scalar residual fusion are established operations; this is an experimental baseline rather than a novel model family.

future_potential.positive: A successful matched comparison would justify further investigation of recent-interest fusion while providing interpretable scale and geometry controls.
future_potential.negative: Embedding coherence can reproduce broad topical associations, suppress complementary transitions, and change through shared optimization; improved validation ranking would not establish current intent.

code_difficulty.positive: The architecture requires only causal pooling, item normalization, and one scalar parameter.
code_difficulty.negative: Faithful random-stream matching, controlled ablations, diagnostic adaptation, and generated-predictor parity require more care than the branch itself.

related_work.title: CoDeR+ (2026; supplied search result)
contributions: The supplied summary distinguishes demand shifts from noisy fluctuations, motivating caution about treating all recent interactions as intent.
limitations: Does not establish that embedding coherence identifies current intent in these four datasets.

related_work.title: Scarcelli et al. (2025; supplied search result)
contributions: The supplied summary describes minimal sequence edits that change recommendations, motivating sequence-aware diagnostic interventions.
limitations: Recommendation sensitivity does not establish causal user intent or benchmark improvement.

related_work.title: Pandey et al. (2026 preprint; supplied search result)
contributions: The supplied summary motivates masking-robust temporal attribution and cautions against interpreting raw attention as faithful attribution.
limitations: Deletion effects may reflect unfamiliar inputs; the selected residual does not implement its separately trained attribution probe.

related_work.title: Subbiah et al. (2024; supplied search result)
contributions: The supplied summary discusses negative-sampling rank corrections for ranking objectives.
limitations: Does not validate larger training margins as evidence of improved full-catalog recommendations or validate the proposed residual.

related_work.title: CLSR (WWW 2022)
contributions: Uses separate long/short-term encoders, mean-pooled history proxies for contrastive supervision, and adaptive attention fusion.
limitations: Establishes a close fusion precedent but does not validate cosine-coherence gating of a SASRec residual.

related_work.title: TLSRec (CIKM 2022)
contributions: Combines hierarchical self-attention, short-term session average pooling, and a dimension-wise time-lag gate.
Provides relevant pooling and fusion ablation precedents.
limitations: Its architecture and gating evidence do not establish gains for this lightweight residual.

related_work.title: PAN
contributions: Learns contextual, time-aware short-term interests and gates their fusion with long-term interests.
limitations: Adaptive fusion is established prior work; the supplied evidence does not demonstrate effectiveness on the pinned benchmark.

related_work.title: The Hidden Pitfalls of the Cosine Similarity Loss
contributions: Motivates attention to norm-dependent optimization effects when using cosine-based quantities.
limitations: Cosine-loss analysis does not directly establish the training dynamics or ranking quality of this residual gate.

related_work.title: SimSiam
contributions: Provides a precedent for stop-gradient as a consequential optimization intervention.
limitations: Does not establish that detaching recommendation gates makes them semantically meaningful or freezes shared geometry.

related_work.title: PyTorch reproducibility guidance
contributions: Supports explicit random-state management for controlled comparisons.
limitations: A shared seed alone does not guarantee matched stochastic operations or reproducibility across platforms.

related_work.title: Cawley and Talbot: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains overfitting and selection bias introduced by model-selection procedures.
limitations: Ordinary paired bootstrap intervals do not correct adaptive checkpoint or configuration selection.

related_work.title: Krichene and Rendle: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows why sampled recommendation metrics require care when interpreting full-catalog performance.
limitations: Does not authorize changing the pinned sampled evaluator; full-catalog diagnostics remain separate.

related_work.title: Benchmark variance study (supplied search result)
contributions: Motivates reporting evaluation uncertainty and distinguishing sources of variation.
limitations: User bootstrap intervals conditional on fixed models and candidates omit training-seed variability and selection bias.

related_work.title: PyTorch model saving and loading guidance
contributions: Supports reconstructing the trained architecture, loading its state, and using evaluation mode for inference.
limitations: Correct loading alone does not ensure routing, padding, truncation, score, or ranking parity; explicit checks remain necessary.
